Level 4: Digital logic

NOT gate

Flips its single input: 0 becomes 1, and 1 becomes 0.

What is it?

NOT, also called an inverter, has one input and one output. Its symbol is a triangle with a small circle, the “bubble”, which means inversion. In CMOS it takes just 2 transistors.

What does it do?

The output is always the opposite of the input.

Why it matters

Inverters are everywhere: they turn NAND into AND, create the inverted select line in multiplexers, and chains of them form oscillators.

Real chip

74LS04Hex inverter in one 14-pin packageView the pinout

Real-world illustration. Modern CPUs do not contain 74xx chips. Their gates are transistors only a few nanometres wide, etched directly into the silicon die, with billions on one chip. A 74-series chip shows the same logic at a size you can hold and wire up yourself.

Real-life examples

  • Ring oscillatorAn odd number of inverters in a loop
  • Mux selectCreates the inverted select signal
  • SubtractionInverts the bits of B

Real chip
74LS04 (hex inverter)

How it connects

  • NAND gateAND plus NOT
  • SRAMTwo inverters in a loop store a bit

Fun fact

Connect an odd number of inverters in a loop and the circuit can never settle, so it oscillates. Chip makers use these “ring oscillators” to measure how fast their transistors are.
